outcome: No resolution or partial progress on B(2,5) specifically was found since 26 January 2024; it remains explicitly stated as open in every current source consulted (Wikipedia, Groupprops, Euler Circle expository papers, Encyclopedia of Mathematics). The only nearby movement in the broader Burnside problem — the Atkarskaya–Rips–Tent bound that free Burnside groups B(m,n) are infinite for odd n≥557 — was already present in v3 of that paper (submitted 22 June 2023), before the frozen revision date, and in any case concerns exponent ≥557, not exponent 5, so it does not touch this bullet's stated case.
summary: The bullet asks: for which (m,n) is the free Burnside group B(m,n) finite, in particular is B(2,5) finite? Extensive searching (arXiv, Wikipedia's current article, Groupprops, Encyclopedia of Mathematics, Euler Circle expository slides/papers from 2022 and 2025, and general web search) turned up no result, claim, or partial progress touching B(2,5) or the exponent-5 case since 26 January 2024. The current Wikipedia article (fetched live, for context only — not used as the frozen basis) still states plainly 'The particular case of B(2,5) remains open' and 'when the exponent is small and different from 2, 3, 4 and 6, very little is known.' The one piece of related motion in this area is Atkarskaya, Rips and Tent's result that B(m,n) is infinite for m≥2 and odd n≥557 (arXiv:2303.15997), improving the prior bound of 665. I checked its version history directly: the n≥557 bound was already the stated result in v3, submitted 22 June 2023 — before the window opens — with v4/v5 (March 2024) being later revisions of the same already-announced bound, not a new result. Even setting the date aside, n≥557 is a different case of the general problem (large exponents) from n=5, so it would not count as a change to this bullet's status under the scope rule (§3.1) even if it were newly dated. I also distinguished the free Burnside group B(2,5) (this bullet, unresolved) from the restricted Burnside group RB(2,5), whose finiteness (order 5^34) was settled by Kostrikin's theorem and computed by Wamsley in 1974 — a different, already-resolved object that some pages conflate with B(2,5); this predates the window by decades and is not the free group asked about here. No AI system appears anywhere in the sources I found relevant to the Burnside problem generally, including recent small-cancellation-theory and asymptotic-Burnside-laws papers (2024–2025) and the general AI-mathematics literature (AlphaProof, AlphaEvolve, Lean formalization surveys) which never mention Burnside groups. I agree with the triage's 'none' verdict.
competing_reading: One could argue the 557-bound paper's final journal-of-record version or its v4/v5 arXiv revision (dated after 26 January 2024) should count as a fresh 'event' for the general Burnside problem bullet, since the paper was still being revised in the window and a careful reader dating by 'first written argument' could quibble about which version is the operative one. I reject this because the substantive numerical result (n≥557) did not change between v3 and v4/v5, and the case is exponent≥557, not exponent 5, so it would be `partial`/`progress` on a different case than the one asked about (B(2,5)), and dating rules (§6.3) call for the first public written argument, which was v3 in June 2023.
what_would_settle_it: A preprint, announcement, or computer-search result that explicitly determines whether B(2,5) is finite or infinite, or narrows the exponent bound below 557 into a range that includes or approaches 5, would settle or partially settle this. No such source was found.
